entries.title: Programming vs software engineering
entries.summary: Three differences: time, scale and trade-offs; the phrase 'programming integrated over time' is an internal Google saying; sustainability is the ability to react to valuable changes.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Hyrum's Law
entries.summary: With enough users, every observable behavior is depended on by somebody; hash iteration order example; it can be mitigated, not eradicated.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Beyonce Rule
entries.summary: If the infrastructure breaks something that CI did not test, the change is not to blame; 'test everything you do not want to break'.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Churn Rule
entries.summary: Since 2012 the infrastructure team migrates its users or upgrades in a compatible way; specialists scale better.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Shift left
entries.summary: Finding problems earlier in the workflow costs less; defense in depth.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Costs and decisions
entries.summary: Cost includes financial, resource, personnel, transaction, opportunity and societal costs; decisions with an explicit rationale; revisit decisions when the data changes.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Genius myth and hiding code
keywords: mito do genio e esconder codigo
entries.summary: Engineering is a team effort; hiding code increases risk; bus factor.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Humility, respect and trust
entries.summary: Three pillars: humility, respect and trust; 'you are not your code'; the acronym HRT does not appear in the PDF.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Blameless postmortem
entries.summary: A postmortem documents root cause, impact, actions and lessons; it is not a list of culprits.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Knowledge sharing
entries.summary: Psychological safety as the foundation; challenges (information islands, SPOF, parroting, haunted graveyards); Readability as mentoring through code review (p.52-54).
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Manager, tech lead and servant leadership
keywords: gerente, tech lead e lideranca servidora
entries.summary: The manager leads people; the tech lead leads technology; manager antipatterns (p.70-72); positive patterns (p.73-78).
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: The three Always of leadership
entries.summary: Always Be Deciding, Always Be Leaving, Always Be Scaling.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: GSM and QUANTS
entries.summary: Goals/Signals/Metrics and the five QUANTS components; before measuring, ask whether the result is actionable.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Style rules and guides
entries.summary: Rules are law; guidance is recommendation; five principles (worth the cost, reader, consistency, avoid dangerous constructs, practicalities).
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Rule automation and formatters
entries.summary: Prefer automation; formatters via presubmit; about 90% of C++ rules checkable (2018 estimate); no automatic rejection by change size (p.117).
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Code review flow, LGTM, owners and readability
keywords: fluxo de code review, lgtm, owners e readability
entries.summary: Three approval aspects (LGTM, owner, readability) that may fall on a single person; one LGTM by default.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Small changes
entries.summary: 'Small' is around 200 lines; initial feedback in about a day; about 35% of changes touch a single file.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Code review good practices
entries.summary: 24 business hours for feedback; description with what and why; one reviewer; types of review.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Critique
entries.summary: Simplicity, trust, generic communication and integration; LGTM, Approval and unresolved comments scoring.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Test size and scope
entries.summary: Size (resources) and scope (code verified) are distinct axes; small runs in one process, medium on one machine.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: 80/15/5 test pyramid
entries.summary: Approximate reference: 80% unit, 15% integration, 5% end-to-end (p.156); 80/20 rule on p.165. There is NO 70/20/10 in the book.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Flakiness
entries.summary: Near 1% flakiness tests lose their value; Google's rate is around 0.15%.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Code coverage
entries.summary: Coverage measures execution, not verification; an 80% target tends to become a ceiling.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Sustainable unit tests
entries.summary: Unchanging tests; public API; state instead of interactions; behaviors; no logic; DAMP over DRY.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Larger tests (overview)
entries.summary: SUT, data, action and verification; configuration as the main cause of large outages (p.204).
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Test doubles
entries.summary: Prefer the real implementation; a fake is ideal when the real one will not do; stubbing and interaction testing with caution.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Fakes: owner and fidelity
entries.summary: The team that owns the real implementation should write and maintain the fake; fakes should have tests (contract tests).
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Deprecation
entries.summary: Code is a liability; advisory rarely migrates; compulsory needs a deadline, enforcement and a team; actionable and relevant warnings.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Large-Scale Changes and Rosie
entries.summary: An LSC does not fit in one atomic commit; four phases (authorization, creation, shards, cleanup); Rosie splits the change into shards.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Version control, trunk-based and One-Version
keywords: controle de versao, trunk-based e one-version
entries.summary: Trunk-based as a scalable policy; long-lived dev branches discouraged; One-Version Rule; Piper and OWNERS.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Build systems (tasks vs artifacts)
entries.summary: Artifact-based systems (Blaze/Bazel) give the 'how' to the system; sandbox, remote cache and external dependencies with hashes.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Dependency management (partial)
entries.summary: Models: Nothing Changes, SemVer, bundle and Live at Head; SemVer is a lossy estimate of risk.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Code Search (overview)
entries.summary: Search and navigation tool integrated with Kythe.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Static analysis and Tricorder
entries.summary: New checks should have less than 10% effective false positives; overall rate below 5%; integration into review; there is no 1% target in the book.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Continuous integration and TAP
entries.summary: CB, RC, fast presubmit; TAP handles more than 50,000 changes per day and runs more than 4 billion tests per day.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Continuous delivery
entries.summary: Faster is safer; flag guarding; release trains; staged rollouts.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Henderson's article (2017)
entries.summary: Catalog of practices (repository, hermetic build, code review, testing, release with canary, OKRs); 2015 data.

entries.title: Managing complexity
entries.summary: Managing complexity is the primary technical imperative; essential and accidental difficulties.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Characteristics of a good design
entries.summary: Eleven internal characteristics; fan-out above about seven suggests complexity.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Information hiding
entries.summary: Hide design decisions; two categories of secrets; identify areas likely to change.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Coupling
entries.summary: Size, visibility and flexibility criteria; simple-data, simple-object, object-parameter and semantic types.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Design patterns
entries.summary: Patterns reduce complexity; risks of forcing the pattern and feature-itis.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Other heuristics
entries.summary: Cohesion, hierarchies, contracts, responsibilities, design for test, binding time, central points of control.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Design practices
entries.summary: Iterate, divide and conquer, top-down and bottom-up, prototyping, collaborative design, how much design to do.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Leave It in a Better State (Patrick Kua)
keywords: leave it in a better state
entries.summary: Small improvements on every pass; the PDF does not use the expression Boy Scout Rule (cited only in SWE-G p.56, note 7).
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Restrict Mutability of State (Kevlin Henney)
entries.summary: Restricting mutability reduces defects; immutable objects are thread-safe.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Write Code for Humans not Machines (Mario Fusco)
entries.summary: Clear names; short methods (about 15 lines), one responsibility, about 3 parameters: numbers from the essay's author.
entries.label: [from source]

entries.title: Implicit Dependencies Are also Dependencies (Klaus Marquardt)
entries.summary: More dependencies than decoupling assumes; changing the meaning of a parameter is changing the interface.

entries.title: Work with a Star and Get Rid of the Truck Factor
entries.summary: Pair rotation to reduce the truck factor.

not_in_book.note: The SWE-G pyramid is 80/15/5 (p.156) and 80/20 (p.165); 70/20/10 is not in the book.
Goodhart's Law does not appear in SWE-G.
The nit: prefix is not described in Critique (SWE-G p.279-288).
The 1% target is not in the book; the criterion is less than 10% (p.292) and the overall rate is below 5%.
CitC does not appear in the SWE-G PDF; workspaces are mentioned on p.283.
The Code Complete sample does not contain the 7 +- 2 rule; only fan-out above about seven (CC2 p.46).
The 97TH (Extended) PDF does not contain the essay The Boy Scout Rule; only SWE-G p.56 (note 7) cites it as an essay of the O'Reilly book. The PDF essay is Leave It in a Better State (97TH p.90).
The cohesion taxonomy is in Chapter 7 of Code Complete, outside the sample.
There is no cyclomatic complexity limit in the sources.
Outside the corpus of this collection.
The canary figures from the v1 package are not in the sources; SWE-PREV (p.10) only describes canary servers.
